- Foreign students who earn an associate degree or higher in Taiwan can apply to extend their stay in the country for up to two years. [1]
- During the extended stay, graduates can work without obtaining a separate work permit. [1]
- Family members of the graduate can also apply to remain in Taiwan during the extended stay. [1]
- During the extended stay, graduates are not subject to restrictions on the types of professional or technical jobs they can take, employer qualifications or minimum salary thresholds. [1]

- The employer must submit a labor insurance and labor pension combined application form (勞保、勞退2合1加保申報表) to the Labor Insurance Bureau on the day the student starts work. [1]
- If the employer fails to report the student to the Labor Insurance Bureau on the day the student starts work, they will be fined 4× the labor insurance premium and 10× the employment insurance premium, and must compensate the student for any loss of benefits. [1]
- The employer should fill out the form (勞保、勞退2合1加保申報表) and submit it to the Labor Insurance Bureau. [1]
- If the student works part‑time or in shifts, the employer must indicate “part‑time” on the form. [1]

- A bachelor's degree takes four years to complete. [1]
- You must earn at least 128 course credits in total. [1]
- Your department may require more credits; check the curriculum table for the exact number. [1]
- For more information, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs (教務處課務組) at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [1]

- 12 additional graduation credits are required for students admitted on an equivalent qualification from a foreign, Hong Kong, or Macau school that ends at the level of Taiwan's second year of senior high school. [1]
- Military training and physical education do not count toward these 12 credits. [1]
- Students admitted on an equivalent qualification from a foreign, Hong Kong, or Macau school whose graduating grades and schools are equivalent to Taiwan's second year of senior high school must complete 12 more graduation credits, excluding military training and physical education. [1]
- For more details, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs (教務處課務組) at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [1]

- In the first year, you must take at least 16 course credits each semester. [1]
- In the fourth year, you must take at least 9 course credits each semester. [1]
- If you need to take fewer credits, you must obtain approval from your advisor and department head; otherwise you may be dismissed. [1]

- International students must take the full‑year 5‑credit course “Chinese for Overseas Chinese Students” instead of the local students’ 3‑credit Chinese (A) plus 2‑credit Chinese (B) course. [1]
- The 5‑credit course is required for all overseas Chinese and international students. [1]
- Local students normally take 3 credits of Chinese (A) plus 2 credits of Chinese (B), but international students only take the 5‑credit course. [1]
- For more details, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs (教務處課務組) at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [1]

- 6 credits of Mandarin courses at the Language Center [1]
- File for the Chinese course substitution before graduation [1]
- Contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs 教務處課務組 at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw [1]

- Students are required to take five physical education courses in five semesters (including Freshman PE I, Freshman PE II, and three PE interest electives in the following three semesters). [1]
- Any course credit earned from these five PE courses does not count toward the number of course credits required for graduation. [1]
- After the five semesters you may take a 1-credit PE course, which also does not count toward graduation. [1]
- For more information, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs 教務處課務組 at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [1]

- A master's degree requires at least 24 credits, not counting thesis credits. [1]
- You must also take at least one graduate course of 1 credit or more at NCU; waived courses do not count. [1]

- Students admitted directly into a doctoral program must complete at least 34 credits, of which at least 18 must be doctoral-level credits (not counting dissertation credits). [1]
- The requirement is specified in National Central University Study Regulations, Article 58. [1]
- For more details, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs (教務處課務組) at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [1]

- Apply before the add/drop deadline of your first semester. [1]
- If approved, you will skip both semesters of Freshman English and receive 6 credits that count toward graduation. [1]
- Contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs 教務處課務組 at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [1]

- Undergraduates must complete at least 100 service hours on the NCU passport before receiving the degree certificate. [1]
- Check your completed hours on the Service Learning Website (服務學習網) or in the Graduation System (畢業審核系統). [1]
- If you have questions, contact the Center for Service Learning, Office of Student Affairs (學務處服務學習發展中心) at https://service-learning.ncu.edu.tw/. [1]

- Service learning is not listed as a graduation condition for master's and doctoral students. [1]
- Graduation requires completion of all required courses and credits, passing the master's or doctoral degree examination, and receiving satisfactory conduct grades each semester. [1]
- Individual departments may set additional requirements. [1]
- For more details, contact the Center for Service Learning, Office of Student Affairs (學務處服務學習發展中心) at https://service-learning.ncu.edu.tw/. [1]
